item.description: Cedar Ridge wide receiver Carter Copeland (12) advances the ball as Rouse safety Liam Mongold (13) defends as Cedar Ridge football takes on Rouse at Cedar Ridge in Austin on Friday, Sept. 18, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) As Ike Riemenschneider stood near midfield before the coin toss of Rouse's Oct. 22 clash against Hutto, an official took him by surprise. "All the referees know you, they always talk about you," the 6-foot-6, 270-pound senior was told. "They always talk about you, like ‘Have you seen that guy from Rouse? He's huge.'" Riemenschneider doesn't just stand out because of his stature. He's also somewhat of an anomaly within high school football. Riemenschneider converted from tight end to offensive line this season, and now serves as the left tackle for an offense averaging 31.6 points per game. What is unique is that he also handles punter and kicker duties for the Raiders, a role that is stereotypically held by a slender specialist or skill position player. MORE: High school football rankings Riemenschneider, who dubs himself the "Biggest Kicker in Texas" on social media - a fact the Statesman could not verify with certainty - has thrived this fall on the line and with his booming boot. Both aspects of his game will be crucial again Thursday as Rouse (4-5, 2-3) aims to claim the final playoff spot in District 24-6A in a must-win game against East View (4-5, 2-3). "Every week he's getting better," Rouse head coach Mark Hopkins said of Riemenschneider's performance as the team's blindside blocker. "He's grown not just into a guy that's out there trying to figure out what to do, but telling other guys and making sure the calls are right and understanding the big picture of things. So he's doing a really good job." Rouse offensive lineman Ike Riemenschneider (76) kicks a field goal as Cedar Ridge football takes on Rouse at Cedar Ridge in Austin on Friday, Sept. 18, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) An injury leads to a new passion Before Riemenschneider put on pads and a helmet, he was a soccer-loving kid who idolized Swedish striker Zlatan Ibrahimović, an uber-confident star who suited up for many of the sport's European giants, such as FC Barcelona, Paris Saint Germain and Manchester United. But as Riemenschneider grew into a larger frame in middle school, football coaches took notice and swayed him to try the sport. In seventh grade, he ended up breaking his arm, limiting his chances to get on the field. "To combat that, I started to learn how to punt and kick, and it's just stuck ever since," he said. "I really like it, and I'm pretty decent at it." item.title: How the Rockets lost their second game of the season: they couldn't stop LaMelo Ball in final quarter
item.description: Houston Rockets players Fred Vanvleet (5), Kevin Durant (7), Alperen Sengun (28) and Tari Eason (17) talk after a timeout at the Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026. Houston Rockets fell to the Minnesota Timberwolves 117-107. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Down the final stretch of Wednesday night's matchup with the Minnesota Timberwolves, Houston Rockets coach Ime Udoka toggled between a few different lineups. Udoka played his usual starting five - Fred VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Jabari Smith Jr., Kevin Durant and Alperen Şengün - for a little more than two minutes. He went to a small-ball variation with Tari Eason in Şengün's place for about 90 seconds, then put Sengun back in for Smith to close out the final 2:10, according to FadeAway's lineup data. What led to the changes? "Trying to get a stop," Udoka said. ROCKETS MAILBAG: Can Amen Thompson touch the top of the backboard? Houston couldn't get enough stops, giving up 35 points in a fourth quarter it lost by 12 en route to its second defeat of the season, 117-107, at Toyota Center. The Timberwolves, playing without star Anthony Edwards, got a strong late-game showing from point guard LaMelo Ball. Udoka said the Rockets did a good job guarding Ball for about three and a half quarters, and he was right. Ball scored 12 of his 20 points and had two of his six assists in the final seven minutes. "I just think we were too loose on them the whole game and they got going," said Durant, who led Houston with 21 points but was one of three Rockets - along with Şengün and VanVleet - with four turnovers. Giveaways were a major problem Wednesday, with 22 Houston miscues leading to 33 Minnesota points. Udoka said the Rockets had poor awareness when kicking the ball out after touching the paint against a Timberwolves defense that routinely sent help. "I lead by example out there, so I can't be leading the team in turnovers," Durant said. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Three of the biggest threats to a Notre Dame victory over Miami
item.description: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA - OCTOBER 10: CJ Carr #13 of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish runs the ball against the Stanford Cardinal at Notre Dame Stadium on October 10, 2026 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Saturday is rapidly approaching and we are all eager to see how Notre Dame responds to the recent challenge laid before them by the college football playoff committee — beat Miami or plan on watching the playoffs from home. But what obstacles lay in Notre Dame’s way? What are some of the biggest threats to that victory? MISCOMMUNICATION Despite the loss of wide receiver Malachi Toney, Miami still has a potent offense, and the Irish need to play much better on defense than they did against BYU. One of the big issues in that loss was the lack of communication or just plain miscommunication on defense. Assignments were blown, and the Irish looked lost at times. We saw similar things in losses to Miami and Texas A&M last year. If Notre Dame can’t play with more discipline and poise, they could suffer the same fate. THE SLOW START In most pf the games Notre Dame has lost during the Marcus Freeman era, we see that the team tends to come out flat — and more than that even. They’re flat, timid, confused, and even overzealous. They work themselves into a hole, and then spend two or more quarters trying to overcome its beginning nonsense. If the Irish can come out swinging and kind of “catch that groove” early, things should work in their favor, but if not… it will be a much MUCH heavier load (especially with the weight of the stakes of this game). COWARDLY PLAY Don’t do it. Do NOT get regrettably conservative. CJ Carr has that issue during most games, and it’s like he’s too afraid to make a mistake — so he overthrows a guy here and then under throws a guy there. He doesn’t turn the ball over , and that’s definitely important, but in a game like this — he needs to unleash himself. That can be accomplished by Freeman having a conversation with him and Mike Denbrock. In that same conversation, Freeman can remind both that Carr has legs, and despite not using them much this season — maybe Saturday would be a good time to use them a bit more. Don’t be cowards — do something different.

item.title: The Panthers Should Add This Versatile Lineman in the Draft
item.description: COLUMBIA, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 03: Cayden Green #70 of the Missouri Tigers blocks Jeramiah McCloud #91 of the Florida Gators at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Columbia, Missouri. (Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. Today our profile will focus on Missouri Tigers offensive lineman Cayden Green. Bio Green (6’5”, 325 lbs.) was a four star recruit and ranked as the state of Missouri’s second best prospect coming out of high school in 2022. Originally signing with Oklahoma, he started five games for the Sooners at left guard before transferring back to his home state. Green continued to hold down the left guard spot until 2025, when the Tigers moved him to left tackle. In his first year at the position, he allowed only seven pressures across over 350 pass blocking snaps, earning him First Team All-SEC recognition. After missing the first game due to injury, Green has been a stalwart at left tackle for the Tigers, allowing five pressures and zero sacks through five games this year. Strengths/Weaknesses One of Green’s biggest strengths is how naturally he took to the change of position. Usually linemen make the transition outside in, but in his first season moving from guard to tackle he earned All-SEC honors. On top of that, the switch to left tackle happened just two weeks before the 2025 season, showing just how coachable and adaptable he is. Green uses his heavy frame to anchor well and has the athleticism to not get beat around the edge on speed rushes. He is a coach’s dream: finishing blocks and playing through the whistle with a true versatility that will total over 1,500 snaps at guard and tackle in his career. While performing well, Green is still new to the left tackle position. His performance this year has really solidified his ranking among the Draft’s top tackles, but there are still some raw moments. He has also battled injuries the last couple of seasons. Nothing major, but still something that some teams might want to look further into. Projection Green is the epitome of a player that every coaching staff wants. He has the coachability and versatility to immediately start at a minimum of three positions on the offensive line, he is consistent in his performance against SEC competition, and he does not commit penalties (flagged just twice so far this season). As he continues to grow into the position, expect his stock to continue rising through the middle of the first round, potentially higher after teams get to interview him at the Combine. item.title: Orioles news: Rotation needs, possible solutions
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 15: Shane Baz #34 of the Baltimore Orioles in action during the game against the New York Mets at Citi Field on September 15, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello, friends. There are now 139 days remaining until the next scheduled Orioles game. Everyone has their own different level of pessimism for how likely it is that MLB’s owner-imposed lockout of the players will end by then in order to allow the season to begin. How you feel about the Orioles rotation minus Trevor Rogers probably has a lot to do with how much urgency you think the team should have this offseason. The team had a “could have been worse” rotation in 2026 even with Rogers being as good as he was from about June on to the end of the season, finishing 17th in MLB with a 4.24 ERA. Probably half a run separated the Orioles from an actually good rotation. Some of that could have been helped with better defense. Some of it could have been helped by better pitching. As things look right now, the rotation is lined up with Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz, Brandon Young, Cade Povich, and Trey Gibson. That’s what is on FanGraphs projected depth chart and I think it seems like a good enough guess. That’s a bad rotation picture unless Povich or Gibson pulls off a Young-like turnaround into 2027, and it’s not even really guaranteed that Young stays turned around. The needs are pretty much the same as they were going into last offseason. They need to reinforce the front end and they need to reinforce the back end too. Last year, the front end reinforcement was trading for Baz; with a 4.11 ERA, he was no help at the front end. The back end reinforcements were Chris Bassitt and Zach Eflin. The Orioles lost Eflin for the season in the middle of his first start, which isn’t Mike Elias’s fault but that bad luck still hurt the team. Bassitt’s 4.59 ERA didn’t help the back end too much in the aggregate, though he was better after returning from back surgery. They’re going to have to do better about it this year. Does Elias have it in him? If he has it in him, will he be able to show it before the lockout hits in December? These are the questions that will be lingering all month until they are either addressed in some affirmative way or the lockout hits and shows the answer is no. Given his track record, I don’t blame anybody for feeling anxious about it. item.title: Cowboys news: The lack of snaps for George Pickens explained
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images If the Cowboys are going to find themselves in any kind of position to win a bad NFC East division, their defense has got to improve. Multiple players have spoken about the state of the unit, and the solutions don’t seem to be that difficult, but they have to put it all together on the field. One of the big topics around Dallas lately has been wide receiver George Pickens and his playing time, or lack thereof. There’s been speculation as to why this is, but it was recently cleared up by head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Brian Schottenheimer Explains George Pickens’ Lack of Snaps, Targets in Recent Cowboys Games – Mike Moraitis, SI.com The reduction of snaps for Pickens has been very noticeable over the last few weeks. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer breaks down why that’s been the case. “Brian Schottenheimer told me that George Pickens snaps have been limited by his injuries,” Clarence Hill of DLLS Cowboys said. “He has been taken off the field because blocking in the run game.” Schottenheimer added that it “would be poor coaching by me” to keep Pickens off the field for any reason. That checks out because Pickens was added to the injury report in Week 7 due to a shoulder issue and he remained on it through last week. Cowboys defense searching for answers after meltdown loss: ‘Execute on Sunday’ – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The Cowboys defense has had trouble with consistency in 2026. According to defensive tackle Quinnen Williams, the solution is quite simple. item.description: New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II intercepts a pass against the Arizona Cardinals. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants secondary was widely looked at as one of team’s weaknesses coming into the 2026 season. The Giants were widely expected to make a splash to rebuild a unit that disappointed in 2025, but instead they merely brought in cornerback Greg Newsome II. Newsome II was a former first round pick by the Browns, but his career stalled in Cleveland and he was traded by the Browns to the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2025. So he was looked at as a flier at best when he signed a one-year deal with the Giants in the spring of 2026. At least that’s how the media at large viewed him. Newsome still saw himself as a first round corner and was willing to bet on himself if he could land in the right situation. Six games later, Newsome has signed a three-year, $46 million extension to make New York his home through the 2029 season. “I believed wholeheartedly after I signed a one-year,” he said on Wednesday. “I knew the type of person I was, first and foremost. And I knew what type of player I was and I knew that if I just get to the right place, that the money will take care of itself. I feel like when you’re somewhere that you’re wanted, you’re somewhere that you’re loved, everything else takes care of itself. So, I knew this would be the place.” He added that he was very intentional in wanting to come play for John Harbaugh and the New York Giants. “My first thing was fit,” Newsome said. “What coaches know me, and that was the biggest thing. I obviously played against Harbs a lot, so he knew what type of player I was, and I knew what type of coach he was. So, that was kind of my first thing, alright, fit. How did his defenses play in the past? Because that’s going to be kind of how the defense will be playing in New York.” From there, Newsome decided to bet on himself in big market. He knew a “Ravens” style defense would fit his skill set, and that the city would be a fit as well as the coach and system. “So, I figured, how about I sign in one year?” he added. “How about I come to New York and just play in front of a big media outlet? I feel like my personality will be able to show more in this city. item.title: Dolphins' Ollie Gordon II agrees NFL taunting rules 'random and vague'
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II has said repeatedly he should have avoided an unsportsmanlike taunting penalty by being quiet and going back to the huddle. Everyone agreed the penalty was untimely and costly, as momentum shifted and the New England Patriots scored 21 straight points in a come-from-behind win. "I took it too far," Gordon said in the Dolphins locker room, three days after the loss. But how far is too far? While criticism of Gordon after the game was warranted, is it also fair to wonder if his actions were truly worthy of a 15-yard penalty? After all, Gordon did not take a swing at a Patriot. Gordon did not spit on a Patriot. Gordon did not pretend to shoot a Patriot with a musket. All fired up after a 5-yard gain, Gordon excitedly shouted at a Patriots defender. According to the NFL, players should not: stand over an opponent, point or verbally confront an opponent, gesture in an opponents' face, follow an opponent after the play is over or demean or embarrass an opponent with a prolonged demonstration. Seriously? Don't demean or embarrass the opponent? This is professional football! We all want our athletes to be warriors on Sundays between the whistles and Mr. Manners once the play is over. My point? Let these guys show some emotion. Allow some grace. Show some restraint before throwing what could be a game-changing flag. "Sometimes it's hard in the moment," coach Jeff Hafley said of tempering emotion. "And if it's hard for coaches in the moment, imagine how hard it is for a 21-year-old in the moment." Hafley, of course, is going to tell his players to celebrate with teammates and not direct their celebrations at the opponent. In general, it's a good practice. Dolphins edge rusher Chop Robinson, when asked, said he's not worried about an unsportsmanlike penalty for doing his 'Chop' celebration too close to a quarterback; because he wants to do it with his teammates. I asked Hafley and Gordon, essentially, if it is known what can be said and cannot be said within earshot of an official. An analogy could be a baseball manager knowing ― in unwritten fashion, of course ― what will almost always lead to an umpire ejection and a trip to the showers. item.description: Jan 23, 2026; Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; Alex de Minaur of Australia in action against Frances Tiafoe of United States in the third round of the men’s singles at the Australian Open at Rod Laver Arena in Melbourne Park. Mandatory Credit: Mike Frey-Ima… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jim Smith Alex de Minaur needed to win one tennis match. Just the one, as Rafael Jodar had already been eliminated from the Paris Masters, leaving the Australian with an extraordinary opportunity to move into the final qualifying position for the ATP Finals. His opponent was Tomas Martin Etcheverry, the world No. 31, who had never beaten a Top 10 player in 20 previous attempts, hardly an impossible assignment. And yet, de Minaur somehow lost 7-6 6-3 , producing a performance that explains why, despite all his consistency and admirable athleticism, he has never quite established himself among the genuinely elite players in tennis. The most damning statistic? One break-point conversion from 13 opportunities. Etcheverry converted two of three, and sometimes tennis really is that simple. de Minaur’s Paris Collapse Exposed Why He’s Not Elite 13 Opportunities and Nothing to Show The problem was not that de Minaur played an opponent who played extraordinary, unreturnable tennis. Etcheverry was indeed excellent, particularly when it mattered, but he was hardly serving 25 aces and making every ball disappear into the corners. He hit four aces, exactly the same number as de Minaur but what he did exceptionally well was establish control through his first serve, landing 76% of them and winning 71% of those points. De Minaur, meanwhile, managed a miserable 47% first-serve percentage. That alone should have made things difficult, yet the Australian still created 13 break points and converted one. De Minaur’s greatest strength is his ability to extend rallies, absorb pace and force opponents into uncomfortable positions. But those qualities become less useful when an opponent serves confidently and refuses to make mistakes. Too often, the Australian’s approach to important return points seemed based on waiting for Etcheverry to provide an opening rather than creating one himself, and yeah, there is nothing inherently wrong with playing percentage tennis. But when an opponent repeatedly survives break points, there comes a stage when simply putting another reasonably deep ball into the court is not enough. And when de Minaur does attempt to become more aggressive, the problem becomes obvious. He is not naturally equipped to produce the overwhelming first-strike tennis that allows the best players to escape difficult situations. His forehand is improving, but it is hardly a devastating weapon. His serve remains relatively ordinary by elite standards, with his movement still exceptional. item.title: ‘Blue was the more appropriate color’: Colin Cowherd trolls Republicans after midterms
item.description: Colin Cowherd Longtime sports commentator and personality Colin Cowherd usually tries to keep politics off of The Herd , but that doesn’t stop him from dropping the occasional political quip. And on Wednesday, he couldn’t resist taking a shot at Republicans after a brutal election night for the GOP. Democrats took control of both the House and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections, and Cowherd made sure his outfit reflected the results. The Fox Sports host opened his show by explaining that he decided against wearing red, and he warned his staff to get used to seeing him in blue. Cowherd’s ‘Red Wave’ Prediction Ahead of the 2022 midterm elections, Cowherd took to social media to declare that Republicans were about to dominate at the polls. “Red wave is coming Tuesday. Don’t mess w people’s kids. It lands differently — and they will hold a grudge. Can’t blame em. That’s my Ted Talk,” Cowherd wrote at the time . That red wave never came. Republicans did win the House that year, but by a much slimmer margin than many expected, while Democrats held on to the Senate. At the time, Cowherd was roasted by the sports world for the prediction. Cowherd didn’t make any bold predictions ahead of this year’s midterms. But Tuesday night turned out to be a massive night for Democrats, who won control of both chambers of Congress and majority of governorships for the first time in 16 years. ‘Blue was the more appropriate color’ When Cowherd went on air Wednesday, he appeared to take some pleasure in poking at the right. “I was gonna wear a red shirt today, but I woke up and just felt like blue was the more appropriate color,” Cowherd said with a chuckle, in a clip shared by Awful Announcing . “I told the people in the back, I’d get some blue shirts ready for the next two years, it’s just a theme.” This is far from the first time that Cowherd has stirred the pot with a political comment. Over the years, he has praised Kamala Harris for being pleasant, criticized Democrats after their loss in the 2024 presidential election, and called Donald Trump a “ con artist .” He has also described Trump as an “appealing” leader . Clearly, Cowherd knows how to get a reaction from both sides of the aisle. But this time around, he seems pretty happy with how things turned out. item.description: ‘He’s a top player, and we want to get the best of him’ – Folarin Balogun makes welcome Monaco return Folarin Balogun (25) is back in the team and back on the scoresheet. The USMNT forward returned from the FIFA World Cup injured, whilst his aborted move to Everton on transfer deadline day was a considerable distraction. That came after, if not the most prolific, at least the most complete season of his career. He netted 19 goals in 43 games in all competitions for the Principality club, but it was his link-up and work off the ball that also earned him plaudits. Balogun drafted into Monaco’s Conference League squad Due to his knee injury, he missed the start of the season and was subsequently omitted from Monaco’s UEFA Conference League squad. He will therefore be eligible to face Nordsjaelland on Thursday night. Speaking at a press conference attended by Get French Football News, Filipe Luís addressed Balogun’s return: “I think it’s important for Balogun also [to come into the Conference League squad]. item.title: “Not good enough” – Alexander Isak reacts to Liverpool’s loss to Fenerbahce
item.description: “Not good enough” – Alexander Isak reacts to Liverpool’s loss to Fenerbahce Alexander Isak admits Liverpool were lacking after costly Fenerbahce defeat Alexander Isak offered little room for excuses after Liverpool’s perfect Champions League start ended in Istanbul. Twice they took the lead against Fenerbahce. Twice they surrendered it. By the final whistle, a promising position had become a 3-2 defeat. For the Liverpool striker, the frustration centred on an opportunity wasted. Scoring away from home in a demanding atmosphere should have given Andoni Iraola’s side something to build upon. Instead, their inability to protect either advantage allowed the hosts to recover and ultimately take all three points. Speaking to LFCTV, in comments reported by Ian Doyle for the Liverpool Echo, Isak acknowledged that Liverpool had fallen short while resisting the suggestion that the result should provoke panic. Photo: IMAGO Isak delivers honest assessment of Liverpool defeat “It’s never easy but today we could and should have got more out of the game,” Isak said. “It was a bit sloppy that we had the lead twice, and for us to then lose the game is not good enough. Obviously we are going to be disappointed with that.” Trey Nyoni and Isak supplied Liverpool’s goals, but neither breakthrough provided the foundation for a victory. Defensive shortcomings repeatedly undermined their attacking work. That was the central disappointment in Isak’s assessment. Liverpool had done enough to put themselves ahead, yet failed to make those moments count over the course of the match. There is a difference between struggling to establish an advantage and being unable to preserve one. In Istanbul, Liverpool’s problem was the latter, leaving Iraola with questions about how his team manage matches after scoring. Quick responses prevented Liverpool taking control Isak recognised the challenge posed by Fenerbahce’s supporters, but his comments focused on what Liverpool could have done to reduce their influence. “The atmosphere is really good and it’s tough. The one thing you can do to keep them quiet is to score goals,” he said. “It’s a shame we conceded so quickly. We should have capitalised on that and there’s where we were lacking today.” Those immediate responses mattered. Rather than forcing Fenerbahce to spend a prolonged period chasing the game, Liverpool allowed their opponents to regain belief. Protecting a lead does not necessarily require retreating towards your own penalty area. It does require concentration, sound decisions and enough control to prevent the opposition from responding before the game has settled. Liverpool’s failure to achieve that left their goals feeling like brief interruptions to Fenerbahce’s momentum rather than decisive changes in the contest. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo ends Portugal career, federation plans tribute
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo reacts after the 2026 FIFA World Cup group K soccer match between Portugal and DR Congo at Houston Stadium. (is associated with: «Cristiano Ronaldo ends Portugal career, federation plans tribute») Tom Weller/dpa Cristiano Ronaldo has ended his Portugal career with immediate effect, the 41-year-old football star said on social media on Thursday. The forward walked out on the national team during the last international break after a row with coach Jorge Jesus over playing time. He was given a 30-day ban by the Portuguese Football Federation but had been expected to return to the fold for Nations League matches in November. However, he has now decided to call time on an international career which has heralded a men's record 146 goals and a record 234 caps. He first played for the Portugal senior team as an 18-year-old in 2003. "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team," he said in a five-minute video which included clips from across his international career. "I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the honour and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world." Still playing for Al Nassr Ronaldo will still continue to play for Saudi club side Al Nassr as he chases a world record 1,000 career goals, which he could achieve this season. He had previously indicated he could retire completely next year. The Portuguese federation paid tribute to Ronaldo, a Euro 2016 winner and twice Nations League champion. "The Portuguese Football Federation expresses its deepest and most enduring gratitude to its eternal captain, Cristiano Ronaldo, who today announced his permanent retirement from the national team," a statement said. "It is with a sense of deep gratitude and immense admiration that the Portuguese Football Federation publicly honours and thanks Cristiano Ronaldo for his absolutely extraordinary career in the service of our country." A farewell match where he plays seems unlikely given the recent bad blood between the star and coach, but the federation said it was trying to organize a tribute. "The Portuguese Football Federation refuses to let this farewell take place without paying him the tribute he deserves," it added. "It is our firm and heartfelt desire to organize, plan, participate, and actively collaborate in what will always be a tribute worthy of Cristiano Ronaldo's immense career - one in which the fans and the country can once again applaud and celebrate the player who has given us so much." Ronaldo missed out on World Cup glory, unlike his great rival Lionel Messi of Argentina, but will go down in the history books as one of the greatest international footballers of all time.

item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect SUNRISE — Breaking onto a veteran-heavy team that recently won multiple championships like the Florida Panthers isn’t easy, especially if you are a youngster such as Sandis Vilmanis . The rookie forward earned the trust of the Panthers coaching staff over the past few months to land himself a roster spot. Wednesday night was a reward for both of them. In a 5-3 win over the Chicago Blackhawks , Vilmanis showed some star power, ending the night with two goals and two assists for the first multi-goal, and multi-point game of his burgeoning NHL career. “It’s a special night, special night that I will remember for sure,” Vilmanis, 22, said postgame. “Especially thanks to the guys — that just kept me going.” At the 4:43 mark of the first period, Vilmanis opened the scoring after tucking in a cross-crease pass off the rush from Carter Verhaeghe for his second goal of the season. About midway through the second with the Panthers up 2-0, Vilmanis took a page out of Verhaeghe’s book, firing a pass across the top of the paint to set up Seth Jones for Florida’s third goal of the contest. With the Panthers holding onto a 3-2 lead in the third period, Vilmanis rifled a shot short-side past Spencer Knight for his second goal of the game to put his side up 4-2 and sway the momentum back their way. “Ever since we got with him, it’s been pretty great to see kind of the change in his game,” Vilmanis’ linemate Sam Reinhart said. “Just a little bit of confidence goes a long way. Especially when you’re kind of fresh in the league. Nothing but positive things to say about him.” A late Blackhawks goal once again cut the Panthers lead, but Vilmanis was able to chip a puck out of the defensive zone to Reinhart, who put away the empty netter to seal the victory and cap off a 4-point night for the Latvian. “I didn’t put him on the ice with the goalie out for that idea (to complete a hat trick),” Panthers head coach Paul Maurice said. “I just thought that line was out best, and I wouldn’t have been suprised at all [if Vilmanis scored]. But he made the right play … taking it up the wall instead of trying to do it.” Vilmanis is just the third rookie in franchise history to have two goals and four points in a single game ( Jonathan Huberdeau in 2013; Jesse Belanger in 1994). Prior to Wednesday, Vilmanis was yet to have a “break out” game. But that didn’t deter Maurice from putting his youngest player on a line with two elite forwards: Verhaeghe and Reinhart. “Credit to those two veteran players for really working with him,” Maurice said. “They’ve been very positive with him, encouraging — but also teaching [him].” During the injury-riddled 2025-26 season, the Panthers called up Vilmanis in January for his first cup of coffee in the NHL. item.title: Rob Gronkowski names the best offensive player in the NFL
item.description: Photo by Siegfried Anthony/Variety via Getty Images Kay Adams and Rob Gronkowski have been discussing Jaxon Smith-Njigba this week, with the former NFL player offering some high praise. The Seattle Seahawks wide receiver has been unable to prevent his team’s form falling away compared to last season’s Super Bowl-winning campaign. However, when speaking to Adams, Gronkowski has still said that Jaxon is ‘the best offensive player in the game’. He was asked: “Is JSN the only unstoppable player in the NFL?“ Gronk replied: “There’s a couple unstoppable players in the NFL but JSN is at the top of the leaderboard. He’s number one by far. “He’s the best offensive player in the game. His consistency is unreal. This guy is one of the best athletes at the wide receiver position of all time and he’s already proven it and he’s still a super young buck. But what makes him so great is how crisp his routes are. He doesn’t give it away. It looks the same every single route that he runs. It’s hard for a defender to defend JSN because of that. And he’s just so fluid. “His hip mobility, you know, the way he can flip his hips, the way he can break down, it’s just so fluid that it’s so hard to cover and so hard to determine, you know, what type of break, what type of movement he’s going to have, where he’s going to go on the field. And that’s what makes him so great as well. “Also his body control and also his hands going up catching the ball making contested catches not dropping passes. Once in a while drops a pass. Everyone, come on now. Everyone’s human but this guy is one of the best athletes, you know, on the offensive side of the ball in football in quite some time. He really is. He’s phenomenal.” The Seahawks lost to the Chicago Bears on Monday despite JSN managing to lead the game in receiving yards (118). They are now 4-4 going into their meeting with the Arizona Cardinals this weekend, already losing more regular-season games than they did in all of 2025/26 (3). The biggest takeaway is that Klopp is beginning to narrow his option s. After experimenting with 44 players during his first international window, he has made some difficult decisions, rewarding certain players while leaving several established na mes and in-form prospects at home. Raum has been a regular presence in Germany squads and offers experience, attacking quality, and an excellent delivery from the left side. His omission suggests Klopp is willing to rethink his fullback hierarchy rather than automatically relying on established internationals. Kevin Schade – Brentford Schade is a notable omission considering his pace, versatility, and ability to stretch opposing defenses. The Brentford winger was included in Klopp’s original 44-player selection and featured in Germany’s opening Nations League matches. Leaving him out of the November squad suggests Klopp wants to evaluate other attacking options, particularly with Niclas Füllkrug returning and several younger players getting opportunities. Schade will undoubtedly feel he has unfinished business with the national team. There seemed to be a push for Schade to be a part of Germany, but he did not do enough during the last international break to cement his position. The Barcelona attacker was part of Klopp’s initial Germany squad and even started against the Netherlands, but has been left out of the latest selection.
